questions.question: Which of the following elements is present in urea?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, and nitrogen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Urea** is a chemical compound with the molecular formula **CO(NH₂)₂**. It is composed of four main elements: **carbon (C), hydrogen (H), oxygen (O), and nitrogen (N).**
 
• Urea is a significant organic molecule primarily produced in the **liver of mammals** as part of the urea cycle, also known as the ornithine cycle.
 
• In the urea molecule:
 
 
• **Carbon:** Forms the central atom of the molecule, part of the carbonyl group (C=O).
 
• **Hydrogen:** Found in the two NH₂ (amino) groups attached to the central carbon.
 
• **Oxygen:** Present in the carbonyl group (C=O).
 
• **Nitrogen:** Found in the two amino (NH₂) groups.
 
 
 
• It is extensively used in **agriculture as a nitrogen-based fertilizer** due to its high nitrogen content, which is essential for plant growth.
 
• Urea is also utilized in industrial applications like the production of resins, plastics, and cosmetics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chemical Composition of Urea:**

 
 
• Urea consists of **46% nitrogen**, making it one of the most concentrated nitrogen fertilizers available.
 
• The molecular weight of urea is **60.06 g/mol**.
 
• It is highly soluble in water, allowing for quick absorption in agricultural applications.
 
 
 
• **Urea Cycle (Ornithine Cycle):**
 
 
• The urea cycle occurs in the **liver** to convert toxic ammonia, a by-product of protein metabolism, into urea, which is safely excreted through urine.
 
• Enzymes such as **carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I** and **argininosuccinate synthetase** play a critical role in this cycle.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Applications of Urea:**
 
 
• Used in the production of **urea-formaldehyde resins**, which are employed in the manufacturing of particle boards and adhesives.
 
• Plays a role in the **pharmaceutical industry** for synthesizing drugs and medical products.
 
• Commonly used in the creation of cosmetics, particularly in skin creams, as it helps retain moisture.
 
 
 
• **Important Characteristics:**
 
 
• Urea appears as a **white crystalline solid** at room temperature.
 
• It is a non-toxic compound and is biodegradable, making it environmentally friendly when used in proper quantities.
 
• Overuse of urea as a fertilizer can lead to soil degradation and water contamination due to nitrogen leaching.

questions.question: In which city of India was the AIFF-FIFA Football Academy launched in 2023?

questions.question: What is the literacy rate of Schedule Tribes people of India as per Census 2011?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**59%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The literacy rate of Scheduled Tribes (ST) in India, as per Census 2011, stands at **59%**.
 
• This marks a significant improvement from Census 2001, where the literacy rate among STs was recorded at **47.10%**.
 
• The male literacy rate among Scheduled Tribes is higher at **68.5%**, while the female literacy rate is comparatively lower at **49.4%**.
 
• The overall literacy rate of India in Census 2011 is **74.04%**, showing a gap of approximately 14% between the general population and STs.
 
• States like Mizoram and Nagaland report the highest literacy rates among Scheduled Tribes, while states such as Jharkhand and Odisha show relatively lower literacy rates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Challenges Faced by Scheduled Tribes in Education:**

 
 
• Socio-economic barriers such as poverty, traditional livelihoods, and limited access to quality education.
 
• Geographical isolation and lack of educational infrastructure in remote tribal areas.
 
• Language barriers due to differing tribal languages and the medium of instruction.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives for Improving Tribal Literacy:**
 
 
• Programs like the Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) provide educational opportunities for tribal children.
 
• Scholarship schemes like Post Matric Scholarship for ST Students aim to reduce financial burdens.
 
• Focus on skill development and vocational training to empower tribal youth.
 
 
 
• **Definition of Literacy Rate:**
 
 
• The literacy rate refers to the percentage of people aged 7 years and above who can read and write with understanding in any language.
 
• It is calculated based on the total population in this age group.

questions.question: How many Directive Principles of State Policy were added by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 to the original list?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Four**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 added four new Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSPs) to the Indian Constitution.
 
• The newly added DPSPs are aimed at promoting socialism, environmental protection, and equitable justice.
 
• The four newly added principles include:
 
 
• **Article 39:** To secure opportunities for the healthy development of children.
 
• **Article 39A:** To promote equal justice and provide free legal aid to economically weaker sections.
 
• **Article 43A:** To take steps to secure the participation of workers in the management of industries.
 
• **Article 48A:** To protect and improve the environment and safeguard forests and wildlife.
 
 
 
• The amendment was introduced during the Emergency period (1975–77) under the leadership of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.
 
• The 42nd Amendment is often referred to as the "Mini-Constitution" due to the extensive changes it brought, including changes to the Preamble, Fundamental Rights, and distribution of powers between the Centre and States.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSPs):**

 
 
• DPSPs are outlined in Part IV of the Indian Constitution (Articles 36–51).
 
• They are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced by a court of law.
 
• They serve as guidelines for the State in formulating policies to establish social and economic democracy.
 
 
 
• **Other options in the question:**
 
 
• **Option 1 (Two):** This is incorrect as the 42nd Amendment Act introduced four DPSPs, not two.
 
• **Option 2 (Six):** This is incorrect as the number of new DPSPs added was four, not six.
 
• **Option 3 (Seven):** This is incorrect because the amendment did not add seven DPSPs; it added only four.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Protection under DPSPs:**
 
 
• Article 48A, introduced by this amendment, highlights the State's responsibility to protect and improve the environment.
 
• It also aligns with Article 51A (Fundamental Duties), which obligates citizens to contribute to environmental conservation.

questions.question: Which dance form has evolved since the 19th century under the patronage of King Swathi Thirunal of Travancore?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mohiniattam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mohiniattam** is a classical dance form that originated in Kerala, India.
 
• The dance form flourished under the patronage of **King Swathi Thirunal of Travancore** during the 19th century.
 
• It is characterized by **graceful movements, subtle expressions, and feminine themes**.
 
• Mohiniattam is performed as a solo dance by women and is accompanied by Carnatic music.
 
• The term **"Mohini"** refers to the enchanting divine form of Lord Vishnu, which is reflected in the elegance of this dance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **King Swathi Thirunal's Patronage**

 
 
• Swathi Thirunal was a renowned ruler of Travancore and an exceptional composer of Carnatic music.
 
• He played a significant role in reviving and promoting art and culture, including Mohiniattam.
 
• His compositions are still used as musical accompaniments for Mohiniattam performances.
 
 
 
• **Distinctive Features of Mohiniattam**
 
 
• Mohiniattam incorporates **Lasya**, which represents the graceful and delicate aspect of dance.
 
• The costume includes a white sari with golden borders, emphasizing simplicity and elegance.
 
• Movements are soft, rhythmic, and circular, creating a visual representation of feminine charm.
 
 
 
• **Other Dance Forms of Kerala**
 
 
• **Kathakali**: A classical dance-drama characterized by elaborate makeup, costumes, and gestures.
 
• **Theyyam**: A ritualistic dance form performed in temples.
 
• Both Kathakali and Mohiniattam draw inspiration from religious themes and mythology.

questions.question: Vasanthalakshmi Narasimhachari, who won the Nritya Kalanidhi Award 2023, excels in which two dance forms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Vasanthalakshmi Narasimhachari is a celebrated classical dancer, proficient in Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi, two renowned Indian classical dance forms.
 
• She was honored with the Nritya Kalanidhi Award 2023, a prestigious recognition by the Madras Music Academy for her exceptional contributions to Indian classical dance.
 
• Bharatanatyam originates from Tamil Nadu and is distinguished by intricate footwork, graceful movements, and expressive storytelling rooted in Hindu mythology.
 
• Kuchipudi, originating from Andhra Pradesh, is a dance-drama performance art known for its blend of narrative and pure dance accompanied by Carnatic music.
 
• Vasanthalakshmi Narasimhachari, along with her late husband K.P. Narasimhachari, enriched these dance forms by blending tradition with innovative elements and dedicated her life to teaching and preserving them for future generations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sattriya and Mohiniyattam**

 
 
• Sattriya is a classical dance form from Assam, introduced by the saint-scholar Srimanta Sankardeva in the 15th century.
 
• Mohiniyattam is a graceful classical dance form from Kerala, known for its feminine movements and themes derived from Hindu mythology, especially Lord Vishnu.
 
 
 
• **Manipuri and Chau**
 
 
• Manipuri is a classical dance form from Manipur, characterized by gentle, lyrical movements and themes related to Vaishnavism.
 
• Chau is a semi-classical dance drama from eastern India, particularly Odisha, Jharkhand, and West Bengal, blending martial arts and storytelling.
 
 
 
• **Kathak and Odissi**
 
 
• Kathak is a classical dance form from northern India, known for its intricate footwork, spins, and storytelling through rhythmic patterns.
 
• Odissi is a classical dance from Odisha, featuring fluid movements, sculpturesque poses, and themes rooted in Hindu deities and mythology.

questions.question:
Below are few statements about vaccination. Select the correct statement/s.

Statement A:In vaccination, a preparation of antigenic proteins of pathogens or inactivated/weakened pathogens (vaccine) are introduced into the body. Statement B:The vaccines generate memory-B and T-cells that recognise the pathogens quickly.

options.text: Both statements A and B Incorrect
Both statements A and B are correct

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both statements A and B are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Statement A:** Vaccination involves the introduction of antigenic proteins or inactivated/weakened pathogens into the body to stimulate the immune system. This helps the body to recognize and combat pathogens effectively.
 
• **Statement B:** Vaccines lead to the formation of memory-B and T-cells, which are crucial for quick recognition and elimination of pathogens during future infections. This ensures long-term immunity.
 
• Vaccination is a preventive healthcare measure, pivotal in controlling and eradicating diseases like smallpox, polio, and measles.
 
• Memory cells generated during vaccination help the immune system respond faster and more effectively upon re-exposure to the same pathogen.
 
• The development of modern vaccines, such as mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccines, utilizes advanced technologies to maximize efficacy and minimize risks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concept of Vaccination:**

 
 
• Vaccines mimic infection without causing illness, stimulating the immune system to produce antibodies.
 
• They rely on the principle of immunological memory, where memory cells (B and T cells) are created to recognize and neutralize the pathogen during future exposure.
 
• Vaccination also contributes to herd immunity, reducing the overall disease spread within a community.
 
 
 
• **Types of Vaccines:**
 
 
• **Live-attenuated vaccines:** Contain weakened forms of the pathogen (e.g., measles, mumps, rubella vaccines).
 
• **Inactivated vaccines:** Contain killed pathogens (e.g., polio vaccine).
 
• **Subunit/conjugate vaccines:** Include specific parts of the pathogen, such as proteins (e.g., Hepatitis B, HPV vaccines).
 
• **mRNA vaccines:** Use genetic instructions for the body to produce a protein that triggers an immune response (e.g., COVID-19 vaccines).
 
 
 
• **Role of Memory Cells:**
 
 
• Memory-B cells produce antibodies specific to the pathogen upon re-exposure.
 
• Memory-T cells help in detecting and destroying infected cells.
 
• These cells ensure a rapid and efficient immune response, preventing severe illness during subsequent infections.

questions.question: Bismillah Khan, the shehnai maestro, was born in the town of Dumraon which is now located in the Indian state of _______.

• Bismillah Khan is credited with popularizing the shehnai, a traditional Indian wind instrument, and elevating it to the status of a classical music instrument.
 
• He was honored with India’s highest civilian award, the Bharat Ratna, in 2001 for his outstanding contribution to Indian classical music.

• It has contributed significantly to India’s classical dance, music, and Ayurveda practices.
 
• However, Kerala is not associated with the birthplace of Bismillah Khan or the shehnai tradition.

• The state is famous for its folk music and dance forms like Nati, but it does not have any historical connection to Bismillah Khan or the shehnai.

• While Rajasthan has a rich musical legacy, it is not the birthplace of Bismillah Khan or the shehnai tradition.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are INCORRECT?

i. The Government of India launched 'National Agriculture Market' ('e-NAM') Scheme in 2016.

ii. In India, the agriculture credit flow for the year 2020-21 was ₹15,75,398 crore.

iii. The Government of India launched 'National Mission on Edible Oils - Oil Palm' ('NMEO-OP') in 2023.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only iii**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Statement i is correct:** The Government of India launched the National Agriculture Market (e-NAM) Scheme in 2016 to create a unified national market for agricultural commodities by integrating Agricultural Produce Market Committees (APMCs).
 
• **Statement ii is correct:** The agriculture credit flow for the financial year 2020-21 was ₹15,75,398 crore as per the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare data.
 
• **Statement iii is incorrect:** The National Mission on Edible Oils - Oil Palm (NMEO-OP) was launched in 2021, not 2023. It aims to increase domestic production of edible oils and reduce dependency on imports.
 
• Since only Statement iii is incorrect, the correct option is Option 1.
 
• **e-NAM and NMEO-OP:** Both are crucial schemes aimed at improving agricultural infrastructure and making India self-reliant in agriculture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Agriculture Market (e-NAM):**

 
 
• Launched in April 2016 to integrate APMC markets across India, enabling transparent and efficient trade of agricultural commodities.
 
• As of now, over 1,000 mandis are linked to the e-NAM platform, promoting better price discovery and reducing intermediaries.
 
• It empowers farmers with access to nationwide markets, eliminating the limitations of local markets.
 
 
 
• **Agriculture Credit Flow:**
 
 
• Agriculture credit is essential for enhancing productivity and farmer welfare.
 
• The credit flow target has consistently increased over the years, with ₹15,75,398 crore achieved in 2020-21.
 
• This credit is vital for financing inputs, machinery, and other agricultural needs.
 
 
 
• **National Mission on Edible Oils - Oil Palm (NMEO-OP):**
 
 
• Launched in 2021, it aims to boost domestic palm oil production, reducing India's reliance on imports.
 
• The scheme provides financial assistance to farmers for planting materials, inputs, and processing infrastructure.
 
• It is part of India's broader initiative to achieve self-sufficiency in edible oil production.

questions.question: What is the effect of foreign trade on markets?

options.text: It leads to a greater integration of markets.
It makes domestic goods more expensive.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It leads to a greater integration of markets.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Foreign trade promotes **market integration** by linking domestic and international producers, consumers, and suppliers, creating a global marketplace.
 
• It facilitates the **free flow of goods, services, and capital** across borders, enabling access to a variety of products and services worldwide.
 
• Through foreign trade, countries specialize in the production of goods and services where they have a comparative advantage, enhancing **efficiency and economic output**.
 
• Foreign trade enhances **economic interdependence** between nations, encouraging collaboration and reducing the likelihood of conflicts.
 
• It fosters the transfer of **technology, skills, and knowledge**, improving productivity and innovation in domestic economies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Foreign Trade**

 
 
• Foreign trade encompasses the exchange of goods, services, and capital between countries, playing a critical role in **economic globalization**.
 
• It allows countries to benefit from each other's strengths, leading to improved **resource allocation, economic growth, and consumer choices**.
 
• Key components of foreign trade include **exports, imports, and trade policies** like tariffs, quotas, and trade agreements.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Megasthenes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Megasthenes** was an ancient Greek historian, diplomat, and ambassador to the court of Chandragupta Maurya.
 
• He authored the famous work **‘Indica’**, which provides detailed observations on Indian society, administration, geography, and culture during the Mauryan period.
 
• The text **‘Indica’** is considered one of the earliest accounts of India by a foreign traveler and is often quoted by later historians like Strabo and Arrian.
 
• Megasthenes described the Mauryan administrative system, the capital city of Pataliputra, and the social structure of ancient India.
 
• His works highlight key aspects of Indian society, such as the absence of slavery, economic prosperity, agricultural practices, and military organization under Chandragupta Maurya.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Herodotus:**

 
 
• Known as the ‘Father of History,’ Herodotus was an ancient Greek historian who lived during the fifth century BCE.
 
• He authored the work *‘Histories,’* which primarily focused on the Greco-Persian Wars and provided accounts of various cultures and civilizations.
 
• Herodotus did not visit India nor chronicle any observations related to Chandragupta Maurya or the Mauryan Empire.
 
 
 
• **Ptolemy:**
 
 
• Ptolemy was a Greek mathematician, astronomer, and geographer who lived in the second century CE.
 
• He is best known for his works on geography, especially *‘Geographia,’* which provided maps and descriptions of the known world at the time.
 
• While Ptolemy mentioned India in his geographical accounts, he did not serve as an ambassador or provide detailed observations of Indian society during the Mauryan era.
 
 
 
• **Pliny the Elder:**
 
 
• Pliny the Elder was a Roman author, naturalist, and philosopher who lived during the first century CE.
 
• He wrote *‘Naturalis Historia,’* a comprehensive encyclopedia covering various topics, including geography, natural sciences, and history.
 
• Although he mentioned India in his writings, he did not visit Chandragupta Maurya’s court or provide firsthand observations.

questions.question: Which movement was launched in 1942 with the call for 'Do or Die'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Quit India Movement**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Quit India Movement was launched on **8th August 1942** during the All-India Congress Committee session in Bombay (now Mumbai).
 
• It was initiated under the leadership of **Mahatma Gandhi**, who gave the famous slogan **"Do or Die"** to inspire Indians to fight against British rule.
 
• The movement aimed to demand an **immediate end to British colonial rule in India** and pave the way for the country's independence.
 
• The British responded with heavy repression, arresting major leaders like Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, and Sardar Patel, and resorting to mass detentions and violence against protesters.
 
• The Quit India Movement is also known as **August Kranti** and is considered one of the most significant milestones in India's fight for independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Civil Disobedience Movement (1930-1934)**

 
 
• Launched by Mahatma Gandhi, the Civil Disobedience Movement was a campaign of nonviolent resistance against British laws, taxes, and policies.
 
• The movement began with the **Dandi March (Salt March)** on 12th March 1930, where Gandhi led a 240-mile march to produce salt from seawater, defying the British salt tax.
 
• The movement aimed to achieve **self-rule** and included actions like the boycott of British goods, refusal to pay taxes, and non-cooperation with colonial authorities.
 
• It played a significant role in mobilizing Indians across the country but was temporarily suspended after the Gandhi-Irwin Pact in 1931 and resumed in 1932.
 
 
 
• **Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-1922)**
 
 
• The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1920 as a response to the **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre** and the **Khilafat Movement**.
 
• It urged Indians to boycott British goods, institutions, and titles and to adopt swadeshi (use of Indian-made goods) as a form of protest.
 
• The movement gained widespread participation from all sections of society but was abruptly called off by Gandhi in 1922 after the **Chauri Chaura incident**, where a violent mob set a police station on fire.
 
 
 
• **Swadeshi Movement (1905-1908)**
 
 
• Started as a response to the **Partition of Bengal** by Lord Curzon in 1905, the Swadeshi Movement aimed to promote Indian goods and boycott British imports.
 
• This movement marked the beginning of the Indian struggle for economic self-reliance and industrial growth.
 
• It encouraged the use of khadi (handspun cloth) and promoted Indian industries like handloom and textiles while rejecting foreign goods.
 
• Key leaders included Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal, and Lala Lajpat Rai, known as the Lal-Bal-Pal trio.

questions.question: Why is the service industry important in the modern economy?

options.text: It provides raw materials for other industries.
It plays a key role in the provision of activities that aid economic development.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It plays a key role in the provision of activities that aid economic development.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The service industry is a major driver of modern economies, contributing significantly to GDP through sectors like healthcare, education, IT, and finance.
 
• It facilitates the efficient functioning of other industries, such as agriculture and manufacturing, by providing essential support services like logistics, communication, and financial solutions.
 
• Employment generation is a key contribution of the service sector, offering diverse job opportunities across skill levels, from low-skilled jobs in hospitality to high-skilled jobs in IT and finance.
 
• Globalization and advancements in technology have expanded the scope of the service industry, enabling cross-border trade and digital transformation, which further fuels economic growth.
 
• Services such as banking, tourism, and retail not only support economic stability but also foster innovation and competitiveness in the global market.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Importance of the Service Industry**

 
 
• The service sector, or tertiary sector, encompasses industries that offer intangible goods and services, including education, healthcare, finance, and retail.
 
• It is a pivotal component of economic advancement, contributing significantly to GDP and employment creation globally.
 
• By supporting other sectors and fostering innovation, the service industry plays a crucial role in driving sustainable development.

questions.question: Which of the following neighbouring countries of India is secular?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nepal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Nepal** is a secular state as per Article 4 of its Constitution, which was adopted in 2015.
 
• The Constitution ensures that Nepal respects all religions and guarantees equal treatment and protection under the law for every faith.
 
• Secularism in Nepal means that the state does not endorse or favor any religion, providing the citizens with the freedom to practice their religion without interference.
 
• Nepal transitioned to secularism after the abolition of the monarchy in 2008, ending its status as the world's only Hindu kingdom.
 
• The secular nature of Nepal reflects its diverse religious landscape, where Hinduism, Buddhism, Islam, Christianity, and indigenous faiths coexist peacefully.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pakistan:**

 
 
• Pakistan is an Islamic republic, and Islam is declared as the state religion as per its Constitution.
 
• The country's laws and governance are significantly influenced by Islamic principles.
 
• Religious minorities exist in Pakistan, but the state gives preference to Islam in legal and cultural matters.
 
 
 
• **Afghanistan:**
 
 
• Afghanistan is also an Islamic state, and Islam is the official religion as per its Constitution.
 
• The governance system in Afghanistan is heavily influenced by Islamic Sharia law.
 
• Religious freedom is limited, and the state enforces strict adherence to Islamic principles.
 
 
 
• **Maldives:**
 
 
• The Maldives is an Islamic state where Islam is the state religion, and adherence to Islam is a requirement for citizenship.
 
• Non-Muslims are not allowed to practice their religion publicly in the Maldives.
 
• The Constitution mandates that laws must be compatible with the principles of Islam.
 
 
 
• **Secularism:**
 
 
• Secularism is the principle of separating religion from the state, ensuring that governments remain neutral in religious matters.
 
• It guarantees freedom of religion, allowing individuals to practice any faith or none at all without state interference.
 
• Secular states treat all religions equally and do not endorse or discriminate against any religion.

questions.question: Which of the following bodies is authorised to change the name of any state of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parliament**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The authority to change the name of a state in India is vested in the **Parliament of India**.
 
• This power is derived from **Article 3 of the Indian Constitution**, which allows the Parliament to change the name, area, or boundaries of a state.
 
• A **constitutional amendment is not required** for this process, making it relatively straightforward compared to other constitutional procedures.
 
• Before passing the bill for renaming a state, the **President of India refers the proposal** to the respective state legislature for its opinion; however, this opinion is **not binding**.
 
• The final decision is made when the bill is passed by a **simple majority** in both the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Examples of State Name Changes:**

 
 
• **Madras** was renamed **Tamil Nadu** in 1969.
 
• **Bombay** was renamed **Maharashtra** in 1960.
 
• **Orissa** was renamed **Odisha** in 2011 through the Odisha (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2010.

questions.question: A bow, a string, a bracer, a finger tab, a quiver, a bow stand, a bow stringer and a target to shoot at are equipment of _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Archery**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Archery** is a sport where participants use a bow to shoot arrows at a target to earn points based on accuracy.
 
• The essential equipment for archery includes a bow, arrows, a bracer (arm guard), a finger tab, a quiver, a bow stand, a bow stringer, and a target.
 
• A finger tab protects the archer’s fingers from the bowstring, while a bracer shields the forearm from injuries caused by the string’s impact.
 
• Archery has been practiced since ancient times for hunting and combat and has evolved into a popular sport and recreational activity.
 
• Modern archery, particularly recurve archery, is part of the Olympic Games, with a standard target distance of 70 meters for competitors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fencing**

 
 
• Fencing is a sport where participants compete using swords such as the foil, épée, or sabre.
 
• The objective is to score points by striking the opponent on the valid target area with the tip or edge of the weapon.
 
• Fencing equipment includes a sword, protective clothing (jacket, mask, gloves), and scoring sensors.
 
• The sport requires speed, strategy, and precision and has been part of the Olympic Games since their modern inception in 1896.
 
 
 
• **Shooting**
 
 
• Shooting is a precision sport involving firearms or air guns to hit stationary or moving targets.
 
• It includes various disciplines, such as rifle shooting, pistol shooting, and shotgun shooting, with events held over different distances and formats.
 
• Essential equipment includes firearms, ammunition, ear protection, and specialized clothing for stability and comfort.
 
• Shooting is also an Olympic event and requires a high level of focus and hand-eye coordination.
 
 
 
• **Bobsleigh**
 
 
• Bobsleigh is a winter sport where teams slide down an ice track in a gravity-powered sled at high speeds.
 
• The sport requires a combination of physical strength, teamwork, and precision to achieve optimal speed and control of the sled.
 
• Bobsleigh equipment includes a streamlined sled, helmets, and aerodynamic suits.
 
• The sport is contested in the Winter Olympics and is popular in countries with cold climates.

questions.question: The Gulf Stream is a fast, warm ocean current in which ocean?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Atlantic Ocean**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Gulf Stream is a powerful and warm ocean current originating in the **Atlantic Ocean**.
 
• It begins in the **Gulf of Mexico**, flows along the eastern coastline of the United States and Canada, and then moves northeast across the Atlantic Ocean.
 
• The Gulf Stream is part of the larger **North Atlantic Gyre**, a system of rotating ocean currents in the Atlantic Ocean.
 
• This current plays a key role in regulating the climate of the eastern United States and Western Europe, making their temperatures warmer compared to other regions of similar latitude.
 
• The Gulf Stream is driven by **wind patterns** and **thermohaline circulation**, which is based on differences in water temperature and salinity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pacific Ocean**

 
 
• The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean on Earth, covering more than 30% of the Earth's surface.
 
• It is home to several major currents like the **Kuroshio Current** and the **California Current**, which influence the climate of the Pacific Rim countries.
 
• The Pacific Ocean does not host the Gulf Stream; instead, its currents serve different climatic and ecological roles.
 
 
 
• **Southern Ocean**
 
 
• The Southern Ocean encircles Antarctica and is the fourth-largest ocean on Earth.
 
• It is characterized by the **Antarctic Circumpolar Current (ACC)**, which flows eastward around Antarctica and helps regulate the global climate system.
 
• Unlike the Atlantic Ocean, the Southern Ocean does not host warm currents like the Gulf Stream.
 
 
 
• **Indian Ocean**
 
 
• The Indian Ocean is the third-largest ocean and is located primarily in the tropical zone.
 
• It is influenced by monsoonal winds and features major currents such as the **Agulhas Current** and the **Somali Current**.
 
• While the Indian Ocean plays a critical role in weather patterns and marine biodiversity, it is not associated with the Gulf Stream.
